body:
#5840 moved the body of `operator<` into a new `less_general()`, but defined it unconditionally. Before, `operator<` existed only when `JSON_HAS_THREE_WAY_COMPARISON` is off. `less_general()` calls `operator<(value_t, value_t)`, which in C++20 is declared only for GCC (the workaround for GCC bug 105200). Explicit instantiation (`template class basic_json<>`) compiles every member, so clang-cl and MSVC fail in C++20 mode:

```
include/nlohmann/json.hpp(5527,51): error : use of undeclared 'operator<' [test-explicit_instantiation_cpp20.vcxproj]
include/nlohmann/json.hpp(5527,51): error : use of undeclared 'operator<' [test-regression2_cpp20.vcxproj]
```

(from the Windows jobs on #5828, which merged develop)

This PR moves `less_general()` into the `#else` branch of the existing `#if JSON_HAS_THREE_WAY_COMPARISON` around `three_way_general()`. Its only caller, `operator<(const_reference, const_reference)`, is already in the non-three-way branch.

Verified locally: with the GCC-only `operator<` in `value_t.hpp` disabled to mimic a non-GCC compiler, unit-explicit_instantiation fails to compile on develop's `single_include/nlohmann/json.hpp` and compiles with this change. unit-explicit_instantiation, unit-regression2 and unit-comparison are clean under the CI warning flags for GCC 16 and clang (C++11/C++20).

## Public API

No breaking changes. `less_general()` is a private helper.
